newsitem.title: USA: Unisys holder says ISS doesn't back spinoff.
newsitem.headline: Unisys holder says ISS doesn't back spinoff.

text.p: Greenway Partners LP, the largest holder of the common stock of Unisys Corp, said Monday that independent proxy firm Institutional Shareholder Services did not endorse Greenway's proposal for the sale or spinoff of Unisys' computer hardware business.

However, Greenway said ISS has issued a report recommending shareholders vote for the proposal submitted by the Central Fund Pension of the International Union of Operating Engineers calling for the repeal of the company's classified board structure and for the annual election of all directors.
ISS also recommended that shareholders withhold their votes from directors at the annual meeting of Unisys Corp scheduled for April 24, Greenway said.

"Even though ISS did not make it a 'clean sweep' for shareholders by endorsing our proposal to sell or spin off the computer hardware business, we believe ISS in its report has provided enough facts about Unisys for shareholders independently to conclude that the spinoff proposal also warrants support," said Greenway senior managing director Alfred Kingsley.
"We are extremely pleased at the thoughtful ISS report," Kingsley also said. "They have evaluated the performance of Unisys and have quite correctly pointed a finger at this board and management.

"Long-suffering Unisys shareholders should do the same. The vote at the upcoing annual meeting is about accountability for poor results. ISS has endorsed our call to action, our call to withhold votes for directors," he said.
